subject: Pilot infra path qualification and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@playfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot infra path qualification and next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single place to align on next steps and qualification for the pilot. Important notes we captured on the call: 

- Target feature: real-time personalized recommendations on the checkout page.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~200 QPS of inference requests.
- Burst profile: short spikes up to ~600 QPS during promos (5–10 minute windows).
- Latency targets: P50 ~40–60 ms, P95 <= 120 ms.
- Data residency: US-only for PHI-adjacent PII.
- Security: SOC2 required; will need evidence for network isolation and audit logs.

Deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fast on-ramp, flexible), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput), Private VPC (customer-managed network for strict controls). My read from the call: you care most about consistent P95 and predictable bursts; cost is important but secondary to reliable latency during peak windows.

Immediate proposal / asks:
1) Share a short traffic log or synthetic QPS profile (CSV or a 1‑week summary) so our infra team can size the pilot for both steady and burst windows.
2) Approve a 48-hour benchmark pilot on our Hosted API with reserved capacity to validate end-to-end latency under your real traffic. If the pilot shows risk on P95 under burst, we'll propose a Dedicated pool sizing and cost estimate.
3) Confirm any additional compliance gatekeepers (name/email) we should loop in for the SOC2 evidence pack.

I attached a simple SLA matrix template to capture SLOs and a runbook outline for the benchmark.

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute session this week to align on the traffic artifact and lock pilot dates. Are you available Thursday 10–10:30am PT or Friday 9–9:30am PT?

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Kimberly — great summary. A few clarifications / answers from our side: 

- We can provide a 7-day QPS summary exported from our edge (CSV). Steady is ~180–220 QPS, spikes to 550–650 QPS for 6–8 minute promo bursts.
- Target latency: P50 ~50 ms, P95 ideally <100–120 ms (we can tolerate up to 150 ms briefly for very large bursts).
- Data residency: US-only. We are OK with Redwood Hosted provided audit logs and network egress controls meet our compliance team requirements. If not, we'll need a Private VPC.
- SOC2: contact is Jamie Liu (jamie.liu@playfieldhealth.com).

We can do Thursday 10am PT. Please send a calendar invite and a short checklist of what the infra team needs in the traffic CSV.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot infra path qualification and next steps (internal)

Looping in Marissa from Solutions to size the pilot quickly. Quick technical read:

- Given steady ~200 QPS and short spikes to ~650 QPS, default Hosted API will likely meet P50 targets easily but P95 during bursts is the risk vector. Continuous batching and KV caching will help for prefix-heavy workloads, but for tail-latency-sensitive, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) will provide more predictable P95 at cost of commit.
- Recommendation: run a 48-hour hosted pilot with a reserved capacity slot sized for average QPS and a stress benchmark that simulates burst windows. If P95 stays >120 ms under bursts, propose Dedicated sizing (estimate: 4 x A100-style GPUs in a dedicated pool, plus autoscale buffer for peak windows).

Action items for pilot intake (what we need from Playfield):
- 7-day QPS CSV (timestamp, request_type, payload_size_bytes, percent_cache_hit)
- Representative prompt templates and max sequence length
- A sample of typical request/response pairs (sanitized) to validate output correctness and token usage

Attached: benchmark-runbook.md (simple checklist + stress script commands). Marissa — can you confirm availability for a short infra sync on Thursday at 11am PT to define the benchmark knobs?

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming Thursday. 

Summary of agreed next steps and owners: 
1) Playfield: export 7-day QPS CSV + sample request pairs by Wednesday EOD (alex@playfieldhealth.com).
2) Redwood (Ben/Marissa): prepare reserved-hosted pilot config and stress script; run a 48-hour pilot once we receive artifacts.
3) Redwood (Kimberly): send calendar invites for Thursday 10am PT (discovery follow-up) and Thursday 11am PT (infra sync). Also will open a HubSpot deal (DEAL-78341) and attach artifacts.
4) Compliance: Jamie Liu to be added to thread for SOC2 evidence pack; Kimberly to request initial checklist after pilot.

If the 48-hour hosted pilot meets P95 <120ms in bursts, we will proceed with proposal and order form. If it does not, Ben will produce a Dedicated sizing and cost estimate for Playfield to review.

I'll send invites now. Look forward to the pilot.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
